message: In the twin under-deck Tuned Mass Damper (TMD, mass on spring with damper tuned to bridge mode) concept, the tuning basis has apparent conflict between 1.81 hertz and 1.86 hertz. To check it I used the vetted Den Hartog calculation (the Den Hartog optimum result (E3)). I found 1.81 hertz with 64634 newtons per metre stiffness at 13.36 percent damper damping for 5.0 percent mass ratio, according to Den Hartog, 1934. I propose retaining 1.81 hertz as correct for 500 kilograms total mass, thank you Structural Dynamics Lead. My position: ready because tuning is reconciled by mass ratio. In the same twin Tuned Mass Damper concept, the added damping has verification need for comfort. To check it I used two-degree-of-freedom frequency response simulation (the two-degree-of-freedom response simulation (E6)). I found 9.44 percent effective damping rising from 0.4 percent inherent damping, according to Den Hartog, 1947. I propose retaining two 250 kilogram units on coil springs with viscous dampers hung below girders. My position: ready because added damping is quantified. In the 40 metre footbridge retrofit concept, the vertical crowd acceleration has uncomfortable peaks. To check it I used the same response simulation (the two-degree-of-freedom response simulation (E6)) with the maintained under-deck layout (the under-deck twin-unit layout sketch (E7)). I found reduction from 17.50 metres per second squared to 0.74 metres per second squared with 20.0 millimetres travel, reaching Comfort Level (CL, Setra comfort grade) CL2, according to Setra, 2006. I propose accepting concealed midspan twin units with no deck change.
